facts.text: Old Agency was the second Blackfeet Agency from 1879 to 1894, serving the reservation's government affairs.
The complex was built as a defensive stockade with two diagonal bastions and earned the nickname 'Old Ration Place' for its regular food distribution.
In 1879, Indian Agent John Young moved Old Agency's buildings from Upper Badger Creek to a site along the Teton River near Badger Creek.
The 1894 extension of the Great Northern Railway caused the Blackfeet Agency to relocate to Willow Creek, sparking Browning's rise as the reservation's center.
Attempts to shift the Blackfeet from nomadic hunting to farming and ranching began in 1873–1874, but poor soil and mismanagement hampered progress.
After the bison nearly vanished in 1879, Old Agency symbolizes Blackfeet resilience amid lost hunting lands and strained U.S. relations.
